meeting_header:
Date: 2025-06-16
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Omar Salcedo (Redwood CSM), Markus Voss (Silverpine Lead ML Eng), Hannah Lee (Silverpine Infra), Daniel Ortiz (Silverpine CTO), Priya Patel (Silverpine SRE)
summary: Weekly pilot check-in focusing on TTFT (time-to-first-token) and streaming behavior. Reviewed last week's microburst traces, discussed 'conveyor' routing idea for early-response hedging, agreed on targeted tests (10k sample TTFT stress + kernel-selection workshop), and clarified data access for VPC testbed.
topics: 1) Current TTFT numbers and distribution (p50/p95/p99). 2) Streaming vs batched tradeoffs for Silverpine user mix. 3) Kernel choices and sequence-length heuristics. 4) Microburst/multi-tenant noise and hedging. 5) Next steps and permissions.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): All right everyone, thanks for joining. quick sanity check on audio.
[00:07] Markus (Silverpine): Yep, audio's good. we've got about 40 minutes, is that right?
[00:11] Alex: Yup, 42. we'll try to keep things tight. Priya Nair from Redwood is with me, she'll walk the infra traces.
[00:18] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): hey folks. I pulled the microburst profile and a couple of TTFT histograms from the last run — one with streaming enabled and one with streaming disabled.
[00:27] Hannah: quick note, we replayed production like traffic yesterday, about 1.2k qps peak, just so you know the context.
[00:33] Priya: perfect, that helps. ok starting with slide 1 — p50 looks pretty decent ~45ms, p95 around 120ms, p99 at 310ms when streaming is off. with streaming on we got p50 ~40ms, p95 95ms, but p99 is actually a hair worse, 330ms.
[00:50] Markus: Hmm, interesting that p99 is worse with streaming. I expected streaming to always help.
[00:54] Priya: yeah same thought, but what happens is re-assembly cost and microbursts — some streams wait for the next chunk while others are auto-batched and end up waiting on kernel path winstow or something. there's also KV cache warmup spikes.
[01:09] Alex: can you unpack 'conveyor' for us? we sketched something last week about hedging early-response path — is that what you're seeing?
[01:16] Priya: yes. conveyor is our mental model: think of request entering a multi-lane conveyor — early fast lanes for small seqlen low-kv hits, slower lanes for long sequences or cold KV. we can route by predicted seqlen and a quick token-sampled probe.
[01:30] Daniel (CTO): So probe means we send a short prefix first and then decide kernel? isn't that extra round trip?
[01:35] Priya: good q — it's not a full RTT probe, more like internal micro-probing inside the runtime. we look at first few tokens and the tokenizer length, then route locally without external extra RTT. in our tests it nails predicted seqlen about 86% of the time.
[01:50] Hannah: 86% sounds ok but what about the 14% misroutes — do they cost us p99?
[01:55] Priya: that's the tradeoff. misroutes can cause fallback and extra scheduling — which pushes a small tail. but overall for your workload we saw p95 improvements and marginal p99 regressions unless we apply a hedging policy — i.e., when uncertain we fire both fast small-kernel and fallback path but cancel second if first returns within window.
[02:13] Markus: hedging seems expensive though, double compute. does Redwood have a cost estimator for that?
[02:18] Alex: yes we've been prototyping a cost model. Priya, can you speak to the numbers?
[02:22] Priya: sure — hedging cost for the sample set was +18% compute but it reduced p99 from 330ms to 180ms in the critical tail. if you value tail consistency (they're saying product is sensitive), hedging is worth it. without hedging and with conservative routing, p95 improved by 20% and p99 was slightly worse.
[02:42] Daniel: Our customers care about p99 more than cost, so hedging is attractive. however, budget is finite — would prefer selective hedging on sessions that are high-value.
[02:51] Omar (Redwood CSM): we can gate hedging by route or token-level flags, e.g., mark high-priority prompts.
[02:56] Hannah: about kernel choices — last run used the fused-attn kernel on A100s? we actually saw some weird jitter.
[03:02] Priya: good catch. that jitter aligns with kernel fallback we observed: on long sequences the runtime attempted a quantized kernel and then fell back to full-precision kernel for some layers. we should try the seqlen-bucketed kernel selection so long sequences use stable, non-quant paths.
[03:18] Markus: what's the cost hit for non-quant kernel on long sequences?
[03:22] Priya: depends on sequence length. for >1024 tokens, it's about +25% token CPU/GPU time, but p99 becomes stable. for your typical 256 token median, quant path is fine.
[03:33] Alex: can we set a dynamic policy: quant for <512, mixed for 512-1024, full for >1024?
[03:38] Priya: exactly what we prototyped. and then pair that with KV cache warm starters so repeated sessions warm quickly.
[03:46] Hannah: on the VPC test — we granted a temporary role but still need replay data. Markus, did you push the traffic replay?
[03:51] Markus: I started an anonymized dump, but the SRE wanted to scrub a few PII fields. Priya Patel is on it.
[03:56] Priya Patel (SRE): yeah, will send by tomorrow morning. you'll get the replay and an example set of high-priority prompts.
[04:02] Alex: great, that will let us run the 10k TTFT stress test in a near-prod profile.
[04:07] Priya: another observation: microburst behavior changes with client-side batching. some of your clients group requests in the browser and produce sudden bursts — those align with the worst tails. we recommended smoothing client bursts or adding a short jitter at client side.
[04:20] Markus: hmm we can do jitter but it's a product change; might be tough. is there a server-side mitigation?
[04:26] Priya: yes server-side we can enable early-queueing and per-tenant request caps + token-limited preemption. that was the conveyor idea too: a fast lane can only take X concurrent streams, overflow goes to slower lanes gracefully.
[04:39] Daniel: any concerns about multi-tenant noisy neighbor effects? we saw a 30% throughput drop during one noise event.
[04:45] Priya: multi-tenant isolation is real. Dedicated pools or reserved capacity for Silverpine would be best but we also have shaper policies to limit per-tenant microbursts. given this is a POC, we can test both on our hosted infra first.
[04:58] Hannah: Do you have an ETA for the kernel-selection workshop?
[05:01] Alex: we suggested 6/22, is that still okay?
[05:04] Markus: works for us. can you invite the infra folks?
[05:07] Omar: I'll send calendar invite and include an agenda — kernel heuristics, seqlen buckets, hedging windows, and cost tradeoffs.
[05:14] Alex: quick question from the legal/procurement side: Daniel, are you expecting us to run under your VPC or use Redwood Private?
[05:20] Daniel: for now we want to test under our VPC but still prefer Redwood hosted for ease. if results are good we'll evaluate Private later.
[05:28] Priya: ok that's straightforward. we'll run tests in a subnet with the temporary role. Hannah will give access.
[05:33] Markus: about instrumentation — can you dump token-level traces and a mapping to the kernel path for the run? that helped us last week.
[05:39] Priya: yes, we'll include token-timing CSVs and a kernel-path column; expect it in the test artifacts.
[05:45] Hannah: any blockers on Redwood's side?
[05:48] Alex: just two — need the replay and the prompt set, and we need to lock the test window.
[05:53] Markus: we'll provide both by EOD tomorrow.
[05:57] Priya: perfect. one more note: when we did hedging, we set a 25ms cancel window — that gave best tradeoff on cost vs tail. might tweak for you.
[06:07] Daniel: can we use priority tags on API keys so we only hedge high-value customers?
[06:11] Alex: yep, token-level priority is supported; we'll show you how in the kernel workshop.
[06:16] Markus: any competitors we should worry about? we looked at SageMaker endpoints for dedicated but their startup latency looked worse in our bench.
[06:24] Omar: SageMaker is ok for simple endpoints but lacks the conveyor-style hedging and auto KV caching we provide out of the box. OpenAI sometimes has lower p50 but costs and private deployment constraints differ.
[06:35] Hannah: can Redwood add a short doc on recommended client-side jitter and server hedging defaults?
[06:39] Alex: yes, we'll add a short runbook and a config snippet.
[06:42] Markus: summary for next week — run the 10k TTFT test with the replay, try hedging ON/OFF, produce kernel-path traces, and share cost delta.
[06:52] Priya: yep we'll post those artifacts and a short analysis.
[06:55] Alex: thanks everyone. Omar will send the invite for 6/22, and we'll follow up on action items.
[07:00] Daniel: thanks all.
[07:02] Hannah: thanks.
[07:05] [meeting ends]
questions: How to balance hedging cost vs p99 improvements?
Can kernel-selection be automated per-request without extra RTT?
What visibility will Silverpine have into token-level traces in VPC tests?
